messages:
ravi: Weird evening pattern — tokens/sec flattens ~25% below our forecast in eu-west once concurrent requests cross ~4200. GPUs show low util while queue length climbs. Anyone else seeing this?

alex: Yep saw it on grafana around 21:05 UTC, looks like lots of short retries and a bunch of long-seq requests stacking. Dashboard: https://grafana/redwood/d/xyz (short link) :thinking_face:

mira: @ravi can you paste perf counters for one of the affected hosts? want to rule out NVLINK/PCI issues.

ravi: Pasted from host eu-west-node-32: ```gpu0: util=23% avg, mem_used=9G, nvlink_err_count=12, pack_wait_ms=78
gpu1: util=21% avg, mem_used=8.4G, nvlink_err_count=0, pack_wait_ms=81```

ops-bot: :warning: Alert: eu-west inference latency > SLA for service inference-app-1 at 21:12 UTC (auto-detected anomaly)

liam: My hunch is scheduler packing params + request length shift. We're still using max_concurrent_per_gpu=40 but recent traffic has a heavier tail of 2x token lengths -> batching gaps increase and pack_wait grows. Lowering max_concurrent could reduce wasted cycles.

alex: If we reduce max_concurrent we might lower overall throughput but recover steady tokens/sec. Another lever is prioritizing short requests at the scheduler (cheap wins). Need a quick sim though.

mira: Quick sim results (ran locally): `./simulate_capacity --traffic-profile=last_7d --seq-dist=tail-heavy` -> baseline shows 18% tokens/sec drift vs forecast; with max_concurrent=32 drift -> 8%; with max_concurrent=32 + prefetch_kv enabled -> 3%.

ravi: Rough cost impact if we keep current config vs change? how many extra GPU hours to hit SLA?

liam: Back-of-envelope: to regain lost tokens with no config change we'd need ~+14% GPU hours month-over-month. With max_concurrent=32 it's ~+4%. Prefetch_kv adds negligible infra but needs runtime toggle. Gist with numbers: https://gist.github.com/anon/abc123

alex: Proposed plan: 1) canary config change in eu-west (max_concurrent_per_gpu=32) tonight 2) enable prefetch_kv on canary 3) monitor tokens/sec, queue depth, pack_wait_ms for 1 hour 4) rollback if p95 latency > 300ms or error rate climbs. @mira can you run the canary? @ops-bot please open an incident. :clipboard:

mira: On it. Scheduling canary at 22:00 UTC, will post metrics.

ravi: Also please add pack_wait_ms to per-gpu metric export — that'll help correlate.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4321 — eu-west token throughput drift (link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-4321)

mira: 22:15 update: canary rolled to 5 nodes in eu-west. Early results: tokens/sec recovered ~9%, GPU util increased to ~62% on canary hosts, no NVLINK errors observed yet. queue depth reduced by ~18%.

liam: Good signal. After 1h looks stable on canary. Recommend keeping config and rolling to 30% of eu-west while we tune pod-scheduler to prefer short-weighted requests.

alex: I'll open a PR for the scheduler policy + docs: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/909 (draft).

ravi: Thanks all. I'll build a short cost forecast tomorrow comparing: keep-as-is, canary-config rollout, and full scale-up. Will post numbers in the incident.

mira: Closing loop — will keep monitoring and escalate if drift reappears. :white_check_mark:
